\begin{frame}{The task in one slide}
  \begin{columns}
    \column{0.55\textwidth}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Data:} 100{,}775 scraped bina.az sale listings
            $\to$ \textbf{57{,}421} clean residential rows, 55 features.
      \item \textbf{Task A (regression):} predict $\log(\text{price})$
            --- our \textbf{decision tree}, MSE criterion.
      \item \textbf{Task B (classification):} premium vs.\ standard at
            the \emph{train} median (208{,}000 AZN) --- our
            \textbf{Pegasos SVM} + tree in classification mode.
      \item \textbf{Golden rule kept:} both models are our own NumPy;
            scikit-learn appears only as the baseline.
    \end{itemize}
    \column{0.45\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{fig_geo.png}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Cleaning a real dump (decisions, not magic)}
  \begin{columns}
    \column{0.52\textwidth}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Keep \emph{latest scrape} per listing: $100{,}775 \to 64{,}454$.
      \item Residential categories only (units differ elsewhere): $\to 58{,}452$.
      \item Parse Azerbaijani strings: ``145 m\textsuperscript{2}'',
            ``7 / 9'', ``1.3 sot'' $\to$ numbers.
      \item Fixed rule-based outlier bounds (no quantiles $\Rightarrow$
            nothing leaks): $\to$ \textbf{57{,}421}.
      \item \textbf{Leakage dropped:} \texttt{unit\_price},
            \texttt{total\_price}, identifiers, free text, views.
      \item Missing values: constant + explicit indicator column
            (no fitted statistics).
    \end{itemize}
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{fig_eda.png}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Split and framing}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Seeded 70/15/15 split: \textbf{40{,}195 / 8{,}613 / 8{,}613}.
    \item Tier threshold from the \emph{training} median only; balance
          49.9 / 50.5 / 48.9\,\% premium --- balanced by construction.
    \item All tuning on validation; test touched once per final model.
    \item Metrics: RMSE/MAE/$R^2$ (log and AZN) · precision/recall/F1,
          ROC-AUC, confusion matrix.
    \item One command reproduces everything:
          \texttt{python -m src.run\_all} (seed 42).
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Our decision tree (NumPy)}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item CART-style recursion; \textbf{vectorised split search}: per
          feature sort once per node, score \emph{all} thresholds via
          cumulative class counts / $\sum y, \sum y^2$.
    \item Criteria: Gini, entropy, MSE; sklearn-style weighted impurity
          decrease.
    \item Working stopping rules: \texttt{max\_depth},
          \texttt{min\_samples\_split}, \texttt{min\_samples\_leaf},
          \texttt{min\_impurity\_decrease} (unit-tested).
    \item \texttt{predict\_proba} from leaf frequencies;
          impurity-decrease feature importances.
    \item \textbf{Sanity test:} identical split (feature \emph{and}
          threshold) to sklearn on fully-determined toy examples.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Our SVM: Pegasos, no QP solver}
  \[
    J(\mathbf{w},b)=\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^{2}
    +\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_i \max\big(0, 1-y_i(\mathbf{w}^{\top}\mathbf{x}_i+b)\big),
    \qquad \eta_t = \tfrac{1}{\lambda t}
  \]
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Mini-batch (64) sub-gradient updates; bias unregularised;
          features standardised with train statistics.
    \item Margin you can see: $\|\mathbf{w}\| = 3.83$, width
          $2/\|\mathbf{w}\| = 0.52$; \textbf{11{,}693 / 40{,}195 (29\%)}
          training points are support vectors.
    \item Non-linearity: \textbf{random Fourier features} ($D{=}300$) ---
          keeps training $O(nD)$ and reuses the same solver (kernel
          Pegasos would be $O(n)$ per prediction at $n{=}40$k).
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Tuning: the bias--variance story}
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.8\linewidth]{fig_tree_depth.png}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Train RMSE falls monotonically; validation bottoms at
          \textbf{depth 14} $\Rightarrow$ classic overfitting beyond.
    \item Gini vs.\ entropy: nearly identical (F1 0.9242 vs.\ 0.9225);
          Gini chosen on validation.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

  \begin{tabular}{@{}lccc@{}}

\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Why the numbers agree --- and where they don't}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Tree $\equiv$ sklearn to 3--4 decimals: same objective, same
          stopping rules; residual gap = \textbf{tie-breaking} (equal-gain
          splits, float midpoints), not statistics.
    \item Pegasos $\approx$ SGDClassifier(hinge): same loss, same
          schedule family.
    \item \textbf{Linear beats RBF here} (both ours and sklearn's):
          after one-hot encoding, 38/55 features are binary; the
          premium boundary is near-linear in area + centrality.
    \item Speed: our tree 4.7 s vs.\ sklearn 0.45 s (Cython, same
          $O(FN\log N)$); Pegasos 2.2 s; SVC-RBF needed a 15k subsample
          (16.6 s fit, 11.6 s predict).
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{What the models learned}
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.95\linewidth]{fig_importance.png}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item Both families agree: \textbf{area}, then geography
          (distance to centre, district), then floors/renovation.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Error analysis: where and why they fail}
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=0.9\linewidth]{fig_error_analysis.png}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{60\%} of tier misclassifications lie within
          $\pm$15\% of the 208k threshold --- the label is nearly
          arbitrary there.
    \item Regression error doubles in the luxury decile and in
          peripheral / garden-house districts.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Bonuses}
  \begin{columns}
    \column{0.5\textwidth}
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{P8} Ridge via normal equations: $=$ sklearn to
            $10^{-15}$; RMSE$_{\log}$ 0.303 --- linear can't express
            area$\times$location.
      \item \textbf{P9} Forest of \emph{our} trees (bootstrap +
            per-split $\sqrt{d}$): beats the single tree, tracks
            sklearn's forest.
      \item \textbf{P10} k-means segments + PCA sharpen the error story:
            periphery is hardest.
    \end{itemize}
    \column{0.5\textwidth}
    \includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{fig_rf_curve.png}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Takeaways}
  \begin{itemize}
    \item $\sim$250 lines of careful NumPy \textbf{reproduce
          scikit-learn exactly} on 57k real listings --- the classical
          algorithms are small; the library's edge is engineering.
    \item Honest limits: asking prices (not transactions), Baku-only,
          unused text descriptions, threshold-band noise bounds Task B.
    \item Everything reproducible: seeded, pinned,
          \texttt{python -m src.run\_all}, tag \texttt{v1.0-final}.
  \end{itemize}
